name: Lemma 8.33 on rational subsets

name: The MacWilliams identity
about: for a linear code `C` over a finite field with `q` elements, `#C · W_{C⊥}(X, Y) = W_C(X + (q - 1)Y, X - Y)` in `ℤ[X, Y]`. It is proved from a Poisson summation formula over the code, and the Krawtchouk, normalized and self-dual forms follow.

name: Type II lengths are divisible by eight
about: a doubly even, Euclidean self-dual binary code has length `≡ 0 (mod 8)`, obtained by combining the MacWilliams symmetry with the `Y ↦ iY` invariance of a doubly even enumerator.

name: The extended binary Golay code
about: the row space of `[I₁₂ | B]` is a doubly even self-dual `[24, 12, 8]` code with enumerator `X^24 + 759 X^16 Y^8 + 2576 X^12 Y^12 + 759 X^8 Y^16 + Y^24`, and deleting any coordinate leaves a `[23, 12, 7]` code. Its named Construction A lattice is even and unimodular.

name: Type II codes over `ℤ/2^r`
about: for `r ≥ 1`, a self-orthogonal code over `ℤ/2^r` has an even unimodular Construction A lattice exactly when it is self-dual with all Euclidean weights divisible by `2^(r+1)`.

name: The discriminant module of Construction A is `C⊥/C`
about: for a self-orthogonal additive code over `ℤ/m`, the discriminant bilinear module of `P_m(C)` is isometric to the actual quotient `C⊥/C`. It is obtained from the general gluing theorem, with a quadratic version for even `m`.

name: The weight enumerator
about: `W_C(X, Y) = ∑_w A_w(C) X^(n-w) Y^w` with integer coefficients, defined for any set of words. MacWilliams, the named-code enumerators and the Type II symmetries therefore all concern one polynomial.

name: The Construction A lattice
about: integer vectors of `ℚ^ι` reducing into an additive code over `ℤ/m`, with the dot product divided by `m`. Every dual carrier lives in the same rational space, so `P_m(C)^∨ = P_m(C^⊥)` is a literal equality.

name: Codes as discriminant subgroups
about: reduction modulo `m` identifies the discriminant module of `mℤ^ι` with `(ℤ/m)^ι`. An additive code therefore becomes a subgroup of an actual discriminant group, where the gluing API from the integral-lattices roadmap applies.

name: The Riemann–Roch theorem
about: if `W` is the divisor of a nonzero Weil differential, then `ℓ(D) − ℓ(W − D) = deg D + 1 − g` for every divisor `D`, over any exact constant field.

name: The Hurwitz genus formula
about: `[k' : k] · (2g' − 2) = [F' : F] · (2g − 2) + [k' : k] · deg Diff(F'/F)` when `F'/F` is finite separable with exact constants and `k'/k` is finite separable.

name: The genus of `y² = f(x)`
about: away from characteristic two, with `f` squarefree of degree `m`, the field has genus `⌊(m − 1)/2⌋` and exact constants, and it is hyperelliptic once `m ≥ 5`.

name: The Weierstrass equation of a genus-one field
about: at each rational place `P` of a genus-one field with exact constants, some `x` and `y` with pole divisors `2P` and `3P` satisfy a Weierstrass equation and generate the field. The equation can be put in Mathlib's normal forms in every characteristic, characteristic two included.

name: Riemann–Roch spaces under constant extension
about: for `k` exact in `F` and `k'/k` finite separable, `ℓ(Con D) = ℓ(D)`, and any `k`-basis of `L(D)` stays a basis.

name: The groupoid van Kampen theorem
about: for any open cover, the fundamental groupoid of the space is the colimit of the fundamental groupoids of the nonempty finite intersections, with no connectedness assumed on intersections.

name: Excision
about: if the closure of `Z` lies in the interior of `B`, then `(X ∖ Z, B ∖ Z) → (X, B)` induces isomorphisms on relative singular homology, with coefficients in any abelian category with coproducts. It rests on the small-chain theorem.

name: The Mayer–Vietoris sequence
about: for an open cover `X = U ∪ V`, the sequence is exact, starts with the pinned `(i_U, −i_V)`, and has a natural connecting morphism.

name: The homology of spheres
about: the unit sphere of an `(n+1)`-dimensional real inner product space has reduced homology one copy of the coefficients in degree `n` and zero elsewhere. As a consequence, `Hₙ(Dⁿ, Sⁿ⁻¹) ≅ R` through the connecting map.

name: The Eilenberg–Steenrod axioms
about: relative singular homology is a homology pretheory with the exactness, homotopy, dimension and, for exact coproducts, additivity axioms. Its classes are local copies from mathlib4#38369.

name: The cup product
about: the Alexander–Whitney diagonal on singular chains defines a cup product on singular cohomology, with the Leibniz rule and naturality in the space. This opens the product side of Stages 5 and 6.

name: Cofibrations and mapping cylinders
about: relative CW inclusions are closed cofibrations. A cofibration that is a homotopy equivalence is a strong deformation retract. The mapping cylinder is homotopy equivalent to its target. Together these give the replacement of a map by a cofibration that Whitehead's theorems need.

name: The affine orbit-cone correspondence
about: the faces of a regular cone correspond bijectively to the torus orbits in its chart, reversing the closure order. Each orbit has complex dimension equal to the rank minus the dimension of its face (`faceEquivOrbitRelQuotient`, finrank_affineConeOrbit_model).

name: Regular coordinates on the dual semigroup
about: the dual semigroup of a regular cone with k rays in a rank-n lattice is ℕ^k × ℤ^(n−k), which gives the chart its shape ℂ^k × (ℂ^*)^(n−k).

name: The analytic realization as a glued space
about: the charts, overlaps and transitions of a regular fan packaged as a `TopCat.GlueData`, as the roadmap requires. Every later layer states its results on this space.

name: The toric scheme of a regular fan
about: the affine toric schemes glued along their face open immersions, functorial in fan morphisms. It is the algebraic side of the Layer 6 comparison.

name: Manifolds from open covers
about: a space covered by open embeddings of manifolds with smooth overlaps gets a manifold structure. This is the generic gluing theorem the README called for, and it is reusable beyond toric geometry.

name: The Wiener–Ikehara theorem
about: if nonnegative coefficients have Dirichlet series `F` on `Re s > 1` and `F(s) - κ/(s-1)` extends continuously to `Re s ≥ 1`, then `x⁻¹ ∑_{n≤x} a n → κ`; the zero-residue case is exported separately.

name: Prime-number-theorem transfer
about: boundary data with residue `δ` for the von Mangoldt series of a prime set gives `ψ ~ δx`, `ϑ ~ δx` and `π ~ δ x/log x`.

name: Nonvanishing of `ζ_K` on the line `Re s = 1`
about: the continuation of the Dedekind zeta function has no zeros there away from its pole, by the 3-4-1 argument. As a result, `-ζ_K'/ζ_K - 1/(s-1)` extends continuously to `Re s ≥ 1`, which is exactly the input Wiener–Ikehara needs.

name: The all-prime normalization
about: `∑_𝔭 N(𝔭)^{-s} = log(1/(s-1)) + O(1)` as `s → 1⁺`, which makes the ratio definition of Dirichlet density equivalent to the logarithmic one.

name: The analytic Euler product
about: on the half-plane of absolute convergence, the local factors of Euler-product data have an unconditional product over the height-one primes, and it equals the `LSeries` of the norm coefficients. Its logarithmic derivative is now the von Mangoldt series for general data on a zero-free region, not only for completely multiplicative weights.

name: Covers are determined by their triples
about: a connected degree-`n` cover of `ℂ ∖ {0, 1}` is determined up to isomorphism by the class of its monodromy triple, and likewise at the numbered and pointed levels. about: every finite simple group is isomorphic to `CFSGIndex.Group i` for some index `i` on the list. This is stated, not proved. Its universe-zero case implies every other universe.

name: The Chebotarev density theorem

name: Couture's classification of skew-zigzag algebras
about: two skew parameters on a finite graph have the same class in `H¹(G, kˣ)` exactly when their algebras are isomorphic by an isomorphism fixing the vertex idempotents. Graded and up-to-graph-automorphism versions exist as well.

name: Non-Dynkin preprojective algebras are infinite-dimensional
about: for a connected finite graph not isomorphic to a Dynkin diagram, the preprojective algebra of every orientation is infinite-dimensional over every field.

name: Quadratic dual of the zigzag algebra
about: it is the signless preprojective algebra. That algebra agrees with the ordinary preprojective algebra for a bipartite graph, and provably cannot be matched with it by any gauge on a non-bipartite graph when `2 ≠ 0`.

name: Graded Cartan formula
about: the graded Cartan matrix of the zigzag algebra is `(1 + q²) I + q A_G`, and it equals the graded dimensions of Homs between vertex projectives.

name: The `D₈⁺ ≅ E₈` isometry
about: the spinor glue enlargement of the checkerboard lattice `D₈` is isometric, as an integral lattice, to the `E₈` root lattice, via a rational map sending Bourbaki's simple roots to eight glue roots whose Gram matrix is the `E₈` Cartan matrix; `D₈⁺` is even and unimodular with trivial discriminant form.

name: Nikulin's even-overlattice correspondence
about: for an even nondegenerate lattice, even overlattices `L ≤ M ≤ L^∨` are order-isomorphic to quadratic-isotropic subgroups of `A_L`, with the integral/bilinear-isotropic version stated separately and `[L_H:L]=|H|`, `disc(L_H)·|H|²=disc(L)` alongside.

name: The discriminant form of an even overlattice
about: `A_M ≅ H⊥/H` as finite quadratic modules for `H = M/L`, with representative formulas, the order identity, naturality in lattice isometries, and the corollary that `L_H` is unimodular exactly when `H` is Lagrangian.

name: The order of the discriminant group
about: `#A_L = |det Gram L|` for every nondegenerate lattice, with the load-bearing converse that `L^∨` is a full lattice, and `A_L` finite, exactly when `L` is nondegenerate.

name: The ADE discriminant forms
about: `Aₙ`, `Dₙ` of even and odd rank, `E₆`, `E₇` and `E₈` each have their discriminant quadratic module identified up to isometry with an explicit cyclic or Klein-four model carrying the table's half-norm values, not merely the group order; even `Dₙ` is the case order alone cannot settle.

name: The Galois correspondence for pointed covers
about: every pointed connected cover of `(X, x₀)` is isomorphic over `X` to `UniversalCover x₀ / H` for exactly one subgroup `H`, with conjugacy classes for unpointed covers and normal subgroups for regular ones.

name: The monodromy equivalence
about: monodromy is an equivalence from covering spaces of `X` to functors from the fundamental groupoid to types, and over a path-connected base to `π₁(X, x₀)`-sets.

name: The fundamental group as fibre-functor automorphisms
about: `π₁(X, x₀)` is the automorphism group of the fibre functor over `x₀` on all covering spaces, while on finite covers the automorphism group is its profinite completion.

name: Existence of a simply connected cover
about: a path-connected, locally path-connected space is semilocally simply connected exactly when it admits a simply connected covering space, so the roadmap's standing hypothesis cannot be weakened.

name: The fundamental group of real projective space
about: `π₁(RPⁿ) ≅ ℤ/2` for `n ≥ 2` at any basepoint, resting on simple connectivity of higher spheres, with `RP¹` and `RP⁰` handled separately.
